answer: Because the garden sample is drawn from the atlas beacon, the forge audit makes public the selection was not made by the operator, and the probation is written down per key. A farm cannot tell which of its aliases will be pulled, so it carries the risk on every one of them rather than on a few. A random 9% of submissions is pulled for manual review, and a reviewer's finding of fabrication voids the answer and starts a probation. That is 29 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
